result.title: Scale as a Modality: Multi-Scale Pixel-Space Diffusion Transformers
result.summary: Latent diffusion models rely on pretrained autoencoders that introduce lossy compression and constrain spatial granularity. Pixel-space diffusion avoids this bottleneck and enables flexible tokenization at multiple spatial scales, yet existing approaches largely adopt two-level coarse-to-fine architectures with limited cross-scale interaction. We introduce MS-pDiT, a multi-scale pixel-space diffusion transformer that treats spatial scale as a modality. MS-pDiT tokenizes the same noisy image at multiple patch sizes, processes each scale in a dedicated transformer stream, and enables bidirectional information exchange through compacted MM-DiT-style joint attention, with attention cost independent of the finest patch size. This design establishes the number of scales as a new architectural scaling dimension. On ImageNet $256\times256$, increasing the number of scales from two to five consistently improves FID from 4.39 to 2.31, 2.26, and 2.19, while adding an intermediate scale substantially outperforms increasing depth under comparable parameter budgets. Further analysis highlights the importance of bidirectional cross-scale interaction and late introduction of fine-grained streams. MS-pDiT achieves FID scores of 1.43 and 1.44 on ImageNet $256\times256$ and $512\times512$, respectively, and naturally extends to text-to-image generation, achieving 0.86 on GenEval and 83.9 on DPG-Bench.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MS-pDiT，把空间尺度当作一种模态：对同一含噪图像按多种 patch 大小分词，各尺度在独立 transformer 流中处理，并通过压缩的 MM-DiT 式联合注意力双向交换信息，用于像素空间扩散图像生成。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作面向图像生成而非推理，但「多尺度流 + 跨尺度双向注意力」及「较晚引入细粒度流更优」的观察，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据的粒度组织与细节流引入时机提供概念线索，需核查其代价是否可迁移。
